policy_changelog.authority: founder authorization 2026-07-28, verbatim: "firstly i would be up for upgrading the rule, but i think we shouldnt rerun today" — rule upgrade + $0 offline re-compose approved; no new paid cells.
policy_changelog.composition_rule: v3 VERBATIM (every threshold, every required stratum, every requirement, every semantics block) + ONE additive requirement: certified_query_subset. No threshold was tuned; no stratum was changed; no bar was relaxed.
differs_from_v3: ADDED requirements.certified_query_subset (additive + CONDITIONAL — the subset branch of corpus_certification_complete fires only when a policy declares it, so a record evaluated under v1/v2/v3 projects a byte-identical verdict).
ADDED certified_query_subset_semantics (the gate contract, verbatim below).

ADDED required_strata[*].qid_list_sha256 + required_strata[*].query_count_committed — the PRE-REGISTERED subset identity, copied verbatim from the frozen scripts/jseval/782-hero/cells.v1.json (§E.8 freeze). Neither key is read by required_strata_exact (utility_claim_policy._required_projection projects a fixed key set), so the required-matrix comparison is unchanged.
policy_changelog.defect_fixed: FREEZE DEFECT #2 (782 run 2026-07-28, incident-ledger.md): corpus_certification_complete required cert.query_count == cell.query_count EXACTLY (utility_claim_policy.py, v3 line 418). The 781 structural certifications certify the 50-query committed gold set; the frozen 782 §E.1 design measures the pre-registered 20-qid leading-prefix subset (--max-queries 20). 50 != 20 on every stratum, so NO run under the frozen design could ever pass that gate — while query_gold_sha256 (the identity that actually chains the certified queries) matched on all three strata. The defect was a count comparison standing in for a subset-identity check.
notes: The gate keys on qid_list_sha256 rather than the sibling selected_query_sha256 because the COMPOSED RECORD can derive the former and cannot derive the latter: campaign_identity.expected_cells carries the measured qid set, but no query TEXT survives into the record. selected_query_sha256 remains the pre-launch content pin, checked by scripts/jseval/782-hero/preflight.py:172-186 against the committed gold cell before any cell is paid for. Both digests are frozen in cells.v1.json §E.8; this policy pins the one a post-hoc verdict can verify.

A subset is never self-certifying: the subset branch additionally keeps (a) query_gold_sha256 == the cell's query_identity.sha256 — the FULL committed gold file's identity, which the harness hashes whole and truncates only the sample rows — and (b) cell.query_count <= cert.query_count. The subset digest is the third leg, not a replacement for either.

policy_changelog.rationale: This is a corpus-description correction, not a threshold/bar change. The certified 781 v2 gold sets (and all 707 English cells) are 100% 1_hop by construction; the v3-DRAFT's 2_hop entry described a multi-schema cohort that was never built. Requiring the presence of a schema absent from the corpus is a spec error, and the refusal gate surfaced it PRE-SPEND, exactly as intended (782 §G.1's stated residual limit: 'a schema absent from a cell's query set entirely still fails schema_strata_reported ... detectable pre-launch from the committed 20-qid list'). Without this amendment all three hero strata would have failed schema_strata_reported at compose and the full $300 would have bought an unpromotable record.

certified_query_subset_semantics._note: tempdoc 782 §J / FREEZE DEFECT #2. Fixes a certification gate that refused every legitimate pre-registered SUBSET run. Additive and conditional: the branch fires only when requirements.certified_query_subset is declared.
certified_query_subset_semantics.unchanged_when_counts_match: If cert.query_count == cell.query_count the gate evaluates EXACTLY as it did under v1/v2/v3 — a full-count run needs no subset identity, because query_identity.sha256 == cert.query_gold_sha256 together with query_identity.row_count == query_count already pins the whole certified set.
certified_query_subset_semantics.subset_rule: If cell.query_count < cert.query_count the gate passes only when ALL of: (a) cert.query_gold_sha256 == cell.query_identity.sha256 (the FULL committed gold file still chains — the harness hashes the whole file and truncates only the sample rows, so a rewritten subset file fails here); (b) cell.query_count <= cert.query_count; (c) the cell's DERIVED subset identity equals this policy's pre-registered required_strata[*].qid_list_sha256 for that stratum_id.
certified_query_subset_semantics.derived_subset_identity: Read from campaign_identity.expected_cells (already load-bearing for itt_strata_derived and source_identity_complete): each entry is '<condition>|<seed>|<qid>' and every qid is 'q<ordinal>' with a 0-based ordinal into the committed query file in committed order (agent_utility_inspect.agent_utility_task: Sample(id=f'{c}|q{i}') over rows[:max_queries]). The ordinals must form the leading prefix {0 .. n-1} — the only certification-preserving selection — and n must equal the cell's query_count. The digest is then sha256(utf8(joined + '\n')) over the canonical labels ['q0001', ..., 'q{n:04d}'], byte-identical to the recipe scripts/jseval/782-hero/preflight.py:44-58 uses to freeze qid_list_sha256 from the gold source.
certified_query_subset_semantics.fail_closed: A record whose expected_cells are absent, malformed, non-'q<digits>', not a leading prefix, or of a length other than query_count has NO derivable subset identity and FAILS the gate. So does a stratum with no pre-registered qid_list_sha256 in this policy. There is no permissive default.
certified_query_subset_semantics.not_gated_here: selected_query_sha256 (the sibling §E.8 digest over the selected rows' {qid, query, answer, question_type} content) is NOT checked by this gate: no query text survives into the composed record, so a post-hoc verdict cannot verify it. It stays the PRE-LAUNCH pin, asserted by scripts/jseval/782-hero/preflight.py:172-186 against the committed gold cell before any cell is paid for.
certified_query_subset_semantics.provenance: qid_list_sha256 values above are copied verbatim from the frozen scripts/jseval/782-hero/cells.v1.json (§E.8, frozen at the 782 freeze commit, before any measured cell).

required_schema_strata._note: tempdoc 768 D4: within each required stratum the composed record carries a schema_stratified.by_stratum breakdown keyed on question_type (utility_comparison._default_schema_stratify). v3 requires every schema present in the queries file to be represented and reported; a schema that collapses (e.g. email/1_hop null) is reported as an honest null, never dropped. AMENDMENT 1 (2026-07-28, pre-launch): known_schemas is [1_hop] because the certified hero corpora are 100% 1_hop by construction — see policy_changelog.

hero_tier._note: tempdoc 768 item 6 / 766 §G decision 2: closed-book-at-hero-tier requirement, ratified at sonnet.
hero_tier.closed_book_semantics: The hero-tier campaign MUST include a closed-book arm (no tools AND no documents — pure parametric recall) so the with-tool uplift cannot be attributed to memorized corpus content. The private-synthetic corpus is contamination-hardened, but the closed-book floor is the direct evidence: a near-zero closed-book accuracy at the hero tier is what licenses attributing the with-tool number to retrieval rather than recall. A materially non-zero closed-book accuracy voids the benefit headline for that stratum.

triple_reporting_semantics._note: tempdoc 768 item 6 / 762 §T4: the ITT/per-protocol/completion triple wording constraints. Enforces the 'bridge, don't inflate' rule.
forbidden_headlines: raw absolute accuracy of the haiku arm
any single accuracy ratio off a near-zero base (an infinite/undefined ratio must be reframed as completion-rescue or absolute-lift, never a multiplier)

verified_tool_surface_semantics.supersedes_rule: carried over unchanged from v2 (agent-utility-public-v2): the RATE-based surface gate, not the all-cells-verified rule (766 §D.3 item 3 keeps v2's required_strata_exact + this rate gate ACTIVE; 782 §E.2 R2 carries it into v3 verbatim).
verified_tool_surface_semantics.new_rule: verified_tool_surface passes iff ALL of: (a) cells_total > 0 AND cells_total == the number of attempted with-tool (arm B) cells; (b) surface verification rate (cells_with_mcp_surface_verified / cells_total) >= minimum_surface_verification_rate (0.9), where a verified cell is a with-tool attempted cell carrying an observed hash obtained from status/status-retry evidence; (c) observed_mcp_tool_surface_consistent == true; (d) exactly one distinct observed hash across the arm and it equals the cohort's declared mcp_tool_surface_hash; (e) zero cells carry a DIFFERENT observed hash (and the declared cohort hash is present).
verified_tool_surface_semantics.gate_observed_shape: when this rate threshold is present the verified_tool_surface gate reports observed = {"rate": cells_with_mcp_surface_verified/cells_total, "verified": cells_with_mcp_surface_verified, "total": cells_total} and threshold = minimum_surface_verification_rate, so the rate is visible in the verdict.
verified_tool_surface_semantics.missing_hash: a with-tool cell with no observed hash after Track-1 retry + fallback is a CAPTURE MISS, not a violation — it lowers the verification rate (bounded by 1 - 0.9 = 10%) but does not fail the gate on its own.
verified_tool_surface_semantics.different_hash: a with-tool cell whose observed hash DIFFERS from the declared hash stays FATAL — this is a genuine surface mismatch, never a capture miss, and any single occurrence fails the gate regardless of rate.
verified_tool_surface_semantics.evidence: carried from v2; see tempdoc 755 §A/§B/§F and the 2026-07-18 confirmatory VERDICT record.
